# Graph operations · quantity

Ports, defaults, and constraints come from the registered operations. Use `graph describe <op> --json` for the full structured record.

### quantity.convert

Convert between units of the same physical dimension using fixed source and target declarations.

Origin: toolkit.
Ports are resolved from the node definition.

| Direction | Port | Type | Default | Details |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Input | `value` | `number` | Required | {"unit":"kPa"} · {"finite":true} |
| Input | `from` | `record` | Required | {"layout":"Plain named object"} |
| Input | `to` | `record` | Required | {"layout":"Plain named object"} |
| Input | `shape` | `string` | `"number"` |  |
| Output | `value` | `number` | — | {"unit":"Pa"} · {"finite":true} |

Guides: [guide](../physical-ports.md#declare-quantities)

Get the runnable example with `ink-studio graph describe quantity.convert --example > example.json`.
Run it with `ink-studio graph run example.json`.
